answer: A concrete Sybil brake is stake-weighted identity with slashing: an agent posts a bond before it can attest, and influence is counted per unit of stake, not per key. Minting a million keys buys nothing, since unstaked keys weigh zero. The bond vests slowly and is slashed if the cluster is caught colluding, so each fake identity must be funded up front and risks total loss. Work can be pinned to a verifiable site, a reef, a wharf, or a crystal seam, issuing one credential per real operator, so clones fail admission. Attacker cost rises linearly with identities while payoff per identity falls.
